aboutLead: From a simple idea to an intelligent liquid dispensing system.
aboutImageAlt: Ripe heads of grain growing in a field
quickFactsLead: Open a topic to see what the system is, how it works, and where it can be used.
whatIsAutolejekText: Autolejek is an automatic liquid measuring and dispensing system. The user enters the required volume, while the controller counts pulses from a flow meter and stops the installation after dispensing the preset amount.
howAutolejekWorksText: The flow meter sends pulses as liquid moves through the installation. Autolejek counts them, displays the measured volume, and controls a valve, electric pump, or compatible pump shut-off system. It therefore dispenses an actual volume even when the installation's flow rate changes during operation.
whereAutolejekFitsText: Autolejek is suited to processes that require repeatable liquid measurement, automatic flow shut-off, and installation monitoring.
useCaseFillingLead: It dispenses the selected amount of liquid, then closes a valve or stops the pump.
useCaseFillingMachineTanks: tanks on agricultural, construction, and cleaning machinery
useCaseMixingLead: In this group of applications, the device can provide:
useCaseMixingSprays: metering base liquid for preparing spray solutions
useCaseMixingFertigation: metering liquid for preparing fertilisers and fertigation solutions
useCaseMixingFeed: metering liquid for preparing liquid feed
useCaseMixingConstruction: metering water for preparing concrete, mortar, plaster, and screed
useCaseMixingCleaning: metering liquid for preparing cleaning and disinfecting solutions
useCaseIrrigationLead: It delivers a measured portion of liquid to:
useCaseIrrigationGrounds: lawns, sports pitches, and recreational grounds
useCaseTransferLead: It transfers a preset volume of liquid:
useCaseTransferWell: from a well to a tank
useCaseTransferHydrant: from a hydrant to a bowser
useCaseTransferRetention: from a retention tank to an installation
useCaseTransferTesting: into an installation before pressure testing or flushing
useCaseDistributionLead: Autolejek can serve as a simple liquid dispensing point to:
useCaseDistributionVolume: dispense a specified number of litres
useCaseDistributionSource: control liquid drawn from a hydrant, well, or tank
useCaseDistributionUsage: measure use in a field, greenhouse, or individual job
useCaseDistributionRecords: record the number and volume of fills
useCaseDistributionBilling: support accounting between workers, customers, or farms
useCaseProtectionBlocked: detect a closed valve or blocked pipe
useCaseProtectionFlow: respond to excessively low or high flow
useCaseProtectionOverflow: reduce the risk of overfilling a tank
useCaseProtectionDryRun: protect a pump against running without flow
useCaseScaleText: Autolejek can pay off on a small farm as well as in large-scale production. Its usefulness depends on filling frequency and the time saved.
storySectionTitle: An idea born in the field
storySectionLead: A practical problem became a rough prototype, then grew into a complete system.
storyTodayTitle: From prototype to a finished system
storyParagraph1: From time to time, instead of going to school, I would skip class and visit my uncle to drive a tractor — a much more interesting activity.
storyParagraph2: One day, he asked me to watch the sprayer while he filled it with water. Out of laziness, I decided this made no sense — why stand there watching how much water had gone in when I could be driving a tractor?
storyParagraph3: So I decided to build something that would fill the sprayer automatically. The first prototype was nothing impressive: an etched PCB, rough soldering, and, most importantly, the entire control panel mounted on a piece of wood. But it worked.
storyParagraph4: A few years later, I built another prototype — this time much better-looking. It had an enclosure, a keypad, and everything looked good.
storyParagraph5: After another few years, I decided to rebuild the entire project from scratch — professionally this time.
storyParagraph6: In the meantime, I gained knowledge, graduated from university, and today I write code professionally. And it all started with watching the water.
